body: @fatmcgav , it's useless if you shrink an index with only one shard, so the `Shrink Action` throws the `illegal_argument_exception `, maybe it's not a problem?

> @fatmcgav , it's useless if you shrink an index with only one shard, so the `Shrink Action` throws the `illegal_argument_exception `, maybe it's not a problem?

Agreed that technically, it's useless to try and shrink and index with only one shard. 
However the fact that Elasticsearch reports this as an error condition on the index is also redundant in my opinion.

This is inline with the logic applied in #33275. The only difference here is that I'm using `max_primary_shard_size` rather than a specific value of `1`...

We should handle this better in the event that the calculation decides on the same number of shards as the index currently is. Since a user of ILM may not know exactly the size of the index they have we should try not to error in that case and skip the shrink, similar to how we skip `shrink` if the number of shards is the same as the index currently has.

Shrink operations can be executed based on replicas however, when `max_primary_shard_size` yields the same number of shards for the target (shrunk) index as the source index has the `ResizeAllocationDecider` will kick in thinking we're performing a clone. A clone operation is executed from primaries only so this could block the shrink operation.

We should tackle the case when `max_primary_shard_size` would yield the same number of shards as the source index already has, and skip the shrink action.

issue.title: Skip the shrink step if the number of shards of the shrunk index is the same with the original

issue.body:
This PR extends the existing of functionality of skipping the shrink step in ILM if the `number_of_shards` in the action is the same with the number of primary shards of the original index to also apply when we configure `max_primary_shard_size`.

This should resolve: #80180
